title: Intel has its first customer for its most advanced manufacturing process
gist: A SemiWiki forum repost (from OregonLive) reports Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan saying at the TomorrowX investment conference in Austin that Intel has signed its first customer for its leading-edge 18A process, an unnamed client with undisclosed terms, marking a milestone in Intel's push to become a contract manufacturer.

insights.claim: Intel has signed its first external customer for its leading-edge 18A manufacturing process, CEO Lip-Bu Tan said at the TomorrowX investment conference in Austin.
insights.speaker: Brady
insights.so_what: A first 18A foundry customer is a key de-risking milestone for Intel's contract-manufacturing strategy; watch for follow-on customer wins and revenue disclosure.
insights.quote: We just signed the first customer
insights.locator: Intel said Wednesday that the chipmaker

insights.claim: Intel did not name its first 18A customer or disclose financial terms, and has indicated it generally will not identify individual foundry clients.
insights.speaker: Brady
insights.so_what: Customer anonymity limits investors' ability to size the deal; expect the signal to be validated only indirectly through foundry revenue and capex commentary.

insights.claim: The 18A customer win is framed as a milestone in Intel's long-term effort to become a contract chip manufacturer competing for outside foundry business.
insights.speaker: Brady
insights.so_what: Strengthens the bull case for Intel's foundry pivot, though a single unnamed customer is far from proving foundry-scale economics.
